title: The forgiveness of sins
hook: metanoia means a change of mind, a turning around

segments.voice: Yesterday, the communion of saints, and a stadium full of people cheering. Your line was a great cloud of witnesses. Who did you picture in the stands? Day three hundred eight.

You're driving somewhere you've never been. The map app says turn left; you're sure it's right. You turn right. Ten minutes later, the road narrows, the houses thin out, and a sinking feeling arrives. You know you're going the wrong way. Now you have a choice. You can keep going, pride intact, hoping the road bends back. Or you can pull over, admit it, turn the car around, and head back. That moment, the pulling over, the turning of the wheel, is not dramatic. Nobody claps. But everything after it is different. The creed says, I believe in the forgiveness of sins. And the New Testament word for the way there is today's word. It's a word that has picked up a lot of baggage. Underneath, it's about turning the car around.
screen: `THE WRONG ROAD.` → `PULL OVER, TURN AROUND.` → `A WORD WITH BAGGAGE.`

segments.voice: Repentance, in English, sounds heavy: sackcloth, guilt, someone shouting on a street corner. But the Greek word in the New Testament is metanoia. Meta, change or beyond. Noia, from nous, the mind. A change of mind. A new way of seeing, that turns your life around. The Hebrew prophets used a plainer word still, shuv: turn, return. Ezekiel pleads with the people: "wherefore turn yourselves, and live ye." And the first words of Jesus in Mark's Gospel are: "The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent ye, and believe the gospel." Turn around. Something good is here. Think of the prodigal son, in the pigsty. Luke says simply, "And when he came to himself," he got up and went home. That's metanoia. And look what happens: the father sees him a long way off and runs. The forgiveness was waiting before he'd finished his speech. Here's a piece of history. The Latin Bible of the Western church rendered repent as do penance. When scholars went back to the Greek, some, including Luther, argued that the word meant a change of heart, not only a set of acts. Luther's very first thesis said that Jesus meant the whole life of believers to be repentance. Catholic teaching, for its part, also says the outward acts must come from an inward turning. Churches practice it differently. Catholics and Orthodox, and some Anglicans and Lutherans, confess to a priest and hear words of forgiveness. Protestant churches often confess together in worship, or privately to God. Each pairs the same two things: turn, and be forgiven. This week, we've walked the cross, the descent, the third day, the Spirit, the church, the saints, and now forgiveness.
screen: `METANOIA: A CHANGE OF MIND.` · `SHUV: TURN, RETURN.` · `WHEN HE CAME TO HIMSELF.` · `PENANCE, OR A CHANGED HEART?` · then, large: `TURN YOURSELVES, AND LIVE YE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: turn one small thing around. Settle, and breathe. Think of one small road you're on that you know is heading the wrong way. A habit. A grudge. The way you've been talking to someone. Don't make it big. Just one small thing. See yourself pulling over, and turning the wheel. What's the first stretch of road back? If you pray, you can ask God for forgiveness, and for help with the turn. If you don't, simply decide, gently, on the first step. The bell holds the time.
Repentance. From the Greek metanoia, a change of mind: turning your life around, toward God and toward home.
Your line: turn, and be forgiven. Today, take the first step on the road back, and notice that you don't have to finish the speech. Day three hundred eight.

howItsDone: Christians often confess their sins in a prayer said together at worship; Catholics, Orthodox and some Anglicans and Lutherans also go to individual confession with a priest, and Lent is a season especially set aside for repentance.

original.note: Greek: a change of mind, from meta, change, and nous, mind. The New Testament word for repentance.

trapdoor: what you thought: repentance means feeling terrible about yourself.
what it means: a change of mind that turns your life around, and forgiveness waiting on the road home.
what a scholar hears: metanoia rendered as paenitentiam agite, do penance, in the Latin Bible; a translation question behind Luther's first thesis.

notes: Mark 1:15 are among Jesus's first recorded words in Mark (1:15 follows 1:14's summary). Script says 'the first words of Jesus in Mark's Gospel'. Confirm.

Vulgate 'paenitentiam agite' (Matthew 4:17) and Erasmus's 1516 Greek New Testament; Luther's first thesis paraphrased. Confirm the 'some, including Luther' framing, and that Catholic teaching also stresses interior conversion.
Hebrew shuv (שׁוּב) as root of teshuvah; used here only as a root. Confirm.
Practices of confession described without ranking.
